hypotheses.justification: `[Fintype ι]` follows from the other argument `[Unique ι]`: Mathlib has the global instance `Unique.fintype {α} [Unique α] : Fintype α` (Mathlib/Data/Fintype/Basic.lean:111). If the theorem omits `[Fintype ι]` (via `omit [Fintype ι] in`), `orthonormalBasisSingleton ι 𝕜 h v hv` and its coercion to a function still elaborate, with the Fintype instance found by `Unique.fintype`. This is the same pattern as `[Nonempty α]` next to `[Inhabited α]`. The proof `simp` still works: the simp lemma `orthonormalBasisSingleton_apply` holds for any `Fintype ι` instance, so it rewrites the function to the constant `fun _ => v`. The range of a constant function on a nonempty type (nonempty because of `Unique ι`) is `{v}`. There is no degenerate case: `ι` cannot be empty because of `[Unique ι]`.
